description: Real-world precedent for how long this event's floodwaters actually persisted, from public post-event reporting on the Guaíba river gauge at Porto Alegre. Used only as a qualitative benchmark next to this app's own single-interval recession estimate -- it is never fed into flood detection, site ranking, or the forecast evaluated against the 21 May scene.
gauge: Guaíba river at Porto Alegre (metro-area gauge, not a Canoas site-level measurement)

entries.event: Red alert issued; state-wide flooding begins
Satellite signal scene used by this case study
Guaíba level falls below official flood stage for the first time
Level rises again temporarily, back above flood stage
Guaíba recedes below flood stage for good -- about 33 days after the 29 April red alert, and 32 days after this case study's 6 May satellite signal date

source: "Analyzing the Effect of an Extreme Weather Event on Telecommunications and IT: Insights from 30 Days of Flooding" (PAM 2025 preprint, arXiv:2509.04219)
limitations: Single river gauge for the whole metro area, not an independent per-site drainage measurement. Local drainage infrastructure can keep specific low-lying areas wet well after the river itself recedes. Not a validated ground truth for any one industrial site in the watchlist.
